items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I remember the one with Page, on the street... 'This man is Mr. Page... I said, “Hello Mr. Page.” And he shook my hand and that was it. But that I remember.

ctx.x: But if you do, and you choose to bring this up it would be a small point in his life, “You Got Love” is a very obscure 1931 Benny Moten record which he purports, and he’s a very wise man, I mean this is no challenge to Dan Morgenstern’s magnificence and his majesty, but he says that that’s an uncredited Hot Lips Page vocal, the first Hot Lips Page vocal known. And you listen to the record and it makes a hell of a lot of sense. I played it for Eddie Durham and he states it’s Jimmy Rushing. It’s not Jimmy Rushing.
Yeah you can tell Jimmy Rushing, can’t you?

items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: That’s Jimmy Rushing singing “I Need That Love,” not Lips Page.

ctx.x: But how did you finally determine that?

I learned it. You know this is the punch line of studying for a lifetime. I know now. I’m not anywhere near Eddie Durham but I’m better than I was when I was eleven. And it’s Jimmy Rushing. That’s Jimmy Rushing singing “I Need That Love,” not Lips Page. Eddie Durham, as I said, there are like sixty of these little things and obviously I can’t give them all to your camera but of the sixty — so all sixty I thought I was right, all sixty I thought Eddie Durham was wrong. As it stands now Eddie Durham is right 59…
I see. Well I hope you get to keep that one.
